messages:
maria: heads-up — we see a small perf regression on Dedicated Mistral-7B when the app uses long chat templates with system + user preface. p99 jumped ~8% over the last deploy :thinking:
maria: repro is easiest with the 'support-chat' template (long system + examples). repro link: https://perf.redwood/reports/1983128000
tony: any kernel switch traces? could be kernel-selection choosing byte-fallback path for token borders
maria: yup, profiler shows more byte-fallback invocations and KV cache misses during prompt build. snippet from perf profiler:
```
[2026-03-15 12:14:02] kernel_choice: aten_kernel_fast (prev) -> byte_fallback (now)
kv_cache_hits: 92.4% -> 78.9%
avg_batch_wait_ms: 12.1 -> 14.5
```
joy: interesting — token count variance from the chat template probably changes sequence length distribution => different kernel pick and batching threshold
joy: did we see any RoPE scaling weirdness or head/kv dim mismatch logs? that can increase prefetch churn
sam: i dug into the tokenizer. 'support-chat' includes examples with weird unicode and lots of special tokens. byte-fallback spikes when tokenizer emits many 1-byte vs multi-byte tokens interleaved.
maria: confirmed. sample token stats for the template:
```
avg_tokens: 342
stddev_tokens: 48
byte_fallback_pct: 6.8% -> 18.5% when examples included
```
tony: that aligns. increased byte-fallback => different kernel path that doesn't use optimized KV packing, so more cache thrash.
joy: proposed experiments:
- 1) normalize templates: canonicalize unicode, strip zero-width chars
- 2) pre-tokenize and attach tokenized prefix (server-side) to avoid runtime tokenizer variance
- 3) nudge kernel-picker heuristic: treat <chat-template> prefix as high-prefetch candidate (increase prefetch window)
sam: i like (2) + (3). (2) removes tokenizer nondeterminism and keeps seq len stable. (3) may help reuse kernels across requests.
maria: can we try a canary with kernel-picker tweak only first, to validate impact? low-risk.
tony: I'll deploy a canary on a small Dedicated pool with kernel-picker param: prefetch_ms=25 -> 40, per-route override for 'support-chat'
sam: also want to test head-dim mapping conservative fallback. for Mixtral/Qwen we sometimes map heads->prefetch size heuristically, and when tokenizer changes seq length it flips mapping.
joy: add a metric to trace when head-dim mapping flips during requests. currently it's only in debug logs.
perf-bot: CI profile job finished — baseline vs canary diff (quick): p50: -0.8%, p95: -0.4%, p99: -6.2% on canary with kernel-picker prefetch bump. KV cache hit rate +4.3%.
maria: nice! that's promising. can we reproduce without pretokenize? i.e., only kernel-picker change
tony: canary was kernel-picker only. no pretokenize. we also forced byte-fallback path logging to verify.
sam: good sign. next step: run a runbook test with pretokenize on/off and with template canonicalization. i'll schedule a 2hr soak.
joy: one more note — RoPE scaling: for long templates we sometimes hit effective position wrapping for older RoPE impls; that causes attention kernel to route to a broader, slower kernel. add check to detect kernel routed due to RoPE (flag it)
maria: added a TODO in the ticket to correlate RoPE route with regressed traces.
perf-bot: follow-up perf artifact: https://perf.redwood/artifacts/1983128000/canary-summary.json
maria: thanks everyone. i'll open a tiny RFC to make per-route token-normalization an opt-in feature for Dedicated customers with chat templates. :sparkles:
tony: and i'll keep the kernel-picker change in canary for 24h and report back. :thumbsup:
